status: Experimental Devices UI and peer routing implemented, off by default. Physical Windows-Mac Bluetooth verification remains outstanding.

platforms.Windows: Windowless native RFCOMM connector; requests authenticated and encrypted Bluetooth link; no drivers or console helper. Built locally with static C++ runtime; pure address/service self-test passes.
platforms.macOS: Transient RFCOMM service for OS-paired peers; permission text in helper and app. Intel native build/self-test passed in run 41846587150; Apple Silicon job cancelled while queued. No radio use by CI.

relay: A bounded, credit-controlled multiplexer carries both devices' normal application connections across one byte stream. Local listeners bind only 127.0.0.1; remote opens can target only the configured local CrossPaste port. No arbitrary destination proxy.
routing: Temporary peer-ID routes cover HTTP, file/icon requests and WebSockets without replacing saved LAN addresses. Registered routes work without a network interface. Only relay endpoints receive longer timeouts.
trust: Requires an existing saved key and selected peer identity, then normal encrypted authentication. Bluetooth authentication failure never deletes established pairing. OS permissions and pairing are not automated.
tests: 128 local checks pass: framing, concurrent bidirectional transport, credit control, half-close, disconnect/cancellation, owned-process cleanup, route isolation/replacement, offline discovery, wrong identity, trust preservation and existing sync/telnet regressions. These do not prove a physical Bluetooth link.
remaining: updated all-platform CI and packaged UI verification
